items.reviewNote: Nihongo 102, Beginner 2 Week 1-2 PDF vocabulary. Job: the bare を (o) plus たべます (tabemasu) frame on ばんごはん (bangohan), which this lesson teaches as a word.

items.pronunciation: sumisu san wa doyōbi ni shigoto o shimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 2 (vocabulary): しごとをします had no sentence — しごと appears in the deck only as Lesson 3's しごとはくじからごじまでです, where it is a noun, never as an activity you do.

items.target: スミスさんはにほんしゅをのみますか
items.pronunciation: sumisu san wa nihonshu o nomimasu ka
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 2 (vocabulary): にほんしゅ had no sentence. Also coverage job 3 — the deck's only yes/no 〜ますか question is Lesson 6's いきますか, so no ordinary content verb is ever asked this way. English follows the deck's direct-address convention from Lesson 6.

items.target: ひとりです
items.pronunciation: hitori desu
items.reviewNote: Constructed on EXERCISES VII's pattern. Coverage job 2 (vocabulary): ひとり had no sentence, while ふたり and さんにん both do. Paired with v-nannin-desu-ka and adjacent to it.
items.note: ひとり (hitori) and ふたり (futari) are irregular — they do not take にん (nin). Counting with the suffix only starts at さんにん (san-nin).
items.scene: answering how many are in your party

items.target: きのうなにをしましたか
items.pronunciation: kinō nani o shimashita ka
items.reviewNote: From SPEAKING PRACTICE 2, p. 80 — Nakamura's opening question. The deck has no past-tense なにを question at all in circulation: the one that existed (fib-shuumatsu-nani-shimashitaka) is flagged EXCLUDED. This is the more useful of the two anyway, and it is a verbatim dialogue line rather than a derived one.

items.target: すしをたべます
items.pronunciation: sushi o tabemasu
items.note: を (o) marks what the verb acts on: すし (sushi) is the thing being eaten. The particle is written を but pronounced お (o) — it never appears anywhere except as this marker.
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-3) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Lesson 8's o-particle + tabemasu frame

items.target: きのうべんきょうをしませんでした
items.pronunciation: kinō benkyō o shimasendeshita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 3 (forms): しませんでした is a bare word card with no sentence, and no card anywhere shows a nounを します compound in a negative form, which is where the conjugation is easiest to get wrong.
items.note: In a nounを します verb, only します (shimasu) conjugates — べんきょうを (benkyō o) is untouched.

items.english: Smith-san, what are you going to eat?
items.target: スミスさんはなにをたべますか
items.pronunciation: sumisu san wa nani o tabemasu ka
items.reviewNote: Worked example question from EXERCISES III-B ('Ask and answer what someone will do'). The deck's only なにを question is しゅうまつになにをしますか with the catch-all します — nothing asks なにを with a real content verb, which is the whole point of GRAMMAR 1. English follows the deck's direct-address convention from Lesson 6 (スミスさんはあしたきょうとにいきますか → 'Smith-san, will you go to Kyoto tomorrow?').

items.target: スミスさんはステーキをたべます
items.pronunciation: sumisu san wa sutēki o tabemasu
items.reviewNote: Worked example from EXERCISES III-A ('State what someone will do'). The deck's only present-tense を + たべます sentence is the Target Dialogue one I propose above, which is loaded with three other particles; this is the bare pattern with nothing else in the way. Also sets up the Q&A pair that follows.

items.english: Emma-san bought an umbrella by credit card.
items.target: エマさんはカードでかさをかいました
items.pronunciation: ema san wa kādo de kasa o kaimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 1 (particle): second half of the で-place vs で-means pair. Uses Lesson 4's カード and Lesson 2's かさ, so the only new thing is the ambiguity itself. Kept adjacent to p-depaato-de-kasa-kaimashita.
items.note: Same で (de), different job: here it is the means, not the place. Compare エマさんはデパートでかさをかいました (ema san wa depāto de kasa o kaimashita) — only the noun in front of で changes, and it decides which reading you get.

items.target: いいえ、しません

items.note: ます (masu) → ました (mashita) is the whole of the past tense. There is no separate past form of the noun or the particle.

items.english: Suzuki-san is going to buy water at a convenience store.

items.target: ささきさんは
items.pronunciation: sasaki san wa
items.reviewNote: From TARGET DIALOGUE, explained in NOTES 2, p. 75. The book gives it a dedicated note because it is a reusable conversational move, but it never became a card. Cheap to learn and immediately usable.
items.note: Said with rising intonation. It is the topic particle は (wa) with everything after it dropped — the question just asked is understood to carry over, so this means 'and you, what are you going to do?' Swap in any name.

items.target: すずきさんもかぶきをみます
items.pronunciation: suzuki san mo kabuki o mimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 1 (particle): も had no example with a verb anywhere in the deck. This is the subject slot; p-raamen-mo-tabemashita is the object slot. Builds on the Target Dialogue's かぶきをみます.
items.note: Here も (mo) replaces は (wa), so it is the person that is 'as well', not the activity. Contrast スミスさんはラーメンもたべました (sumisu san wa rāmen mo tabemashita), where も sits on the object instead.

items.english: On Saturday, I'm going to eat tempura in Ginza with Suzuki-san.
items.target: どようびにぎんざですずきさんとてんぷらをたべます
items.pronunciation: doyōbi ni ginza de suzuki san to tenpura o tabemasu
items.reviewNote: From TARGET DIALOGUE — Smith's reply, and the title line of the whole lesson. The deck cards the question (td-shuumatsu-nani-shimasu) but none of the three answers, so the dialogue currently has an opening and nothing else. This is also the only sentence in the lesson that shows the full time/place/object particle stack.
items.note: The lesson's word order in full: person は — time に — place で — object を — verb. Three particles already known (に from Lesson 7, で newly split into its place sense, と from Lesson 6) stack around this lesson's new を.

items.english: What did you eat at the festival?
items.target: おまつりでなにをたべましたか
items.pronunciation: omatsuri de nani o tabemashita ka
items.reviewNote: The book's own worked example for EXERCISES VI ('Ask and answer what someone did at an event'). The deck carded substitution alternative 1 (かいます) as a pair but took only the ANSWER from the printed example — なにもたべませんでした exists as `nanimo-tabemasendeshita` with no question in front of it. This restores the missing half and sits directly before it.

items.target: エマさんはスープをのみませんでした
items.pronunciation: ema san wa sūpu o nomimasendeshita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 2 (vocabulary): スープ had no sentence. The note records a genuine trap the vocabulary card cannot show, and the past negative gives のみます a second form in context.
items.note: Soup takes のみます (nomimasu, 'drink') in Japanese, not たべます (tabemasu, 'eat').

items.english: Suzuki-san is going to eat at a restaurant.
items.target: すずきさんはレストランでたべます
items.pronunciation: suzuki san wa resutoran de tabemasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 1 (particle): second half of the に-vs-で minimal pair, differing only in the particle and the verb it licenses. Kept adjacent to p-resutoran-ni-ikimasu.
items.note: で (de) marks where an action happens. Compare すずきさんはレストランにいきます (suzuki san wa resutoran ni ikimasu): に goes to the place, で does something there.

items.target: すずきさんはおんがくをききます
items.pronunciation: suzuki san wa ongaku o kikimasu
items.reviewNote: The book's own worked example for EXERCISES II-B ('State what someone will listen to'). Same situation as II-A: the deck has alternative 2 (ニュース) but not the printed example, and おんがく is otherwise a bare vocabulary card with no sentence.

items.english: I do it at the library.

items.note: The reply drops べんきょうを (benkyō o) because the question already supplied it, leaving the catch-all します (shimasu) to stand in for the whole activity.

items.pronunciation: doyōbi no shichi-ji ni onegaishimasu
items.reviewNote: From SPEAKING PRACTICE 1, p. 80. Combines Lesson 7's どようびに, Lesson 3's clock times and Lesson 3's day-の-time joining into one real utterance, and nothing in the deck does that. Follows sp-yoyaku-o-onegaishimasu so the reservation call stays in order.
items.note: の (no) joins the day to the time — the same construction as Lesson 3's あしたのよじから (ashita no yo-ji kara, 'from 4:00 tomorrow'). に (ni) then marks the whole thing as the appointed time.

items.target: スミスさんはラーメンをたべました

items.reviewNote: Constructed on Lesson 6's だれとデパートにいきますか. Coverage job 1 (particle): と had three statements in this lesson and no question, and the existing だれと question is tied to いきます — this shows it with an object-taking verb, where と and を have to sit in the same sentence.

items.english: I'd like to make a reservation.
items.target: よやくをおねがいします
items.pronunciation: yoyaku o onegaishimasu
items.reviewNote: From SPEAKING PRACTICE 1, p. 80 — Suzuki's opening request. The deck has よやく as a bare noun but never the line that uses it, so a learner knows the word 'reservation' without being able to ask for one.
items.note: Same [noun] を おねがいします frame as Lesson 1's たなかさんをおねがいします (tanaka san o onegaishimasu) and Lesson 4's カレーとサラダをおねがいします (karē to sarada o onegaishimasu) — one of the most reusable request patterns in the book.

items.target: エマさんはニュースをよみません
items.pronunciation: ema san wa nyūsu o yomimasen
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 3 (forms): member 2 of the よみます four-form set.

items.english: Please give me your name and your telephone number.
items.target: おなまえとおでんわばんごうをおねがいします
items.pronunciation: onamae to odenwa bangō o onegaishimasu
items.reviewNote: From SPEAKING PRACTICE 1, p. 80 — the employee's closing line. The deck has おなまえ and おでんわばんごう as separate bare nouns; this is the sentence they were introduced for, and it is what a learner will actually hear at a counter or on the phone.
items.note: と (to) here is Lesson 4's 'and' joining two nouns, not Lesson 6's 'with' — the whole pair is then marked by を as one object of おねがいします.

Coverage job 2 (vocabulary): バー had no sentence — the deck carded alternative 1 (レストラン) and skipped this one. ホテル appears only in this chapter's exercises, so flag it if you want the word carded separately first.

items.target: エマさんはニュースをよみました
items.pronunciation: ema san wa nyūsu o yomimashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 3 (forms): member 3 of the よみます four-form set. Note the English is the only thing distinguishing it from member 1 in speech — Japanese marks the tense, English 'read' does not.

items.target: スミスさんはアイスクリームをかいませんでした
items.pronunciation: sumisu san wa aisukurīmu o kaimasendeshita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 3 (forms): member 4 of the かいます four-form set, and the form the chapter pairs with なにも in Key Sentence 3.
items.note: The past negative stacks both pieces: ません (masen) then でした (deshita). Compare かいません (kaimasen), which is present.

items.english: I'm going to eat at a restaurant.
items.target: レストランでたべます
items.pronunciation: resutoran de tabemasu
items.reviewNote: The paired answer from EXERCISES V-B. Elliptical (both topic and object dropped), so it carries a hint naming its question. Adjacent to ex-doko-de-bangohan-tabemasu-ka.
items.note: The object ばんごはん (bangohan) is dropped in the reply because the question already supplied it — Japanese leaves out whatever is already understood.

items.english: Suzuki-san is going to a restaurant.
items.target: すずきさんはレストランにいきます
items.pronunciation: suzuki san wa resutoran ni ikimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 1 (particle): first half of a に-vs-で minimal pair. This lesson's new で is the particle most easily confused with Lesson 6's destination に, and nothing in the deck puts the two on the same place noun.
items.note: に (ni) marks where the movement ends up. Nothing happens at the restaurant in this sentence — only the arriving.

items.target: はこねでしました
items.pronunciation: hakone de shimashita
items.reviewNote: From EXERCISES VIII, the printed worked dialogue — the book's own line. Coverage job 2 (vocabulary): はこね had no sentence. The deck already holds the two lines either side of it (ともだちとゴルフをしました and どこでしましたか) so this closes the exchange. Elliptical, hence the hint.

items.note: みます (mimasu) has a one-syllable stem み (mi), so the negative is just みません (mimasen) — shorter than it looks, and no irregularity.

items.pronunciation: nichiyōbi ni tomodachi to kabuki o mimasu
items.reviewNote: From TARGET DIALOGUE — Sasaki's reply, the other half of the exchange. Pairs with ささきさんは above and gives かぶき and みます their only Target Dialogue context; the deck's existing kabuki sentence (fib-suzuki-mimasu-kabuki) is a derived exercise answer, not the dialogue line.

items.english: Sasaki-san is going to see a movie.
items.target: ささきさんはえいがをみます
items.pronunciation: sasaki san wa eiga o mimasu
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 3 (forms): member 1 of a four-form set for みます. Also gives えいが its only sentence — it was carded from EXERCISES II-A's substitution list but never used.

items.target: スミスさんはラーメンもたべました
items.pronunciation: sumisu san wa rāmen mo tabemashita
items.reviewNote: Constructed. Coverage job 1 (particle): minimal pair with v-raamen-tabemashita. Lesson 4 introduced も but only ever with です (あれもさんぜんえんです), so nothing in the deck shows it displacing an object marker — which is exactly where a learner reaches for ラーメンをも.
items.note: も (mo) does not sit next to を (o) — it replaces it. Compare スミスさんはラーメンをたべました (sumisu san wa rāmen o tabemashita): same sentence, and the swap is the whole difference between 'ate ramen' and 'ate ramen as well'.

items.target: たべもの
items.pronunciation: tabemono
items.note: Built from たべる (taberu, 'to eat') + もの (mono, 'thing'); のみもの (nomimono, drink) follows the same pattern from のむ (nomu, 'to drink').
items.reviewNote: Moved from the Nihongo 101 course (lesson-2) by the 2026-08-24 absorption; see docs/designs/nihongo-absorption-2026-08.md. Placed here because: Lesson 8 is the eating and drinking lesson

The existing fib-omatsuri-nani-kaimashitaka is the same pattern but with a place; this is the bare form and a verbatim dialogue line.
